title: The book
summary: What the book covers and how it grows.
description: The content itself. The book is never done: notes are added and revised as interests and understanding change, and chapters arrange them for reading.

requirements.text: The book covers the topics in `book.topics`.
Any part of the book can be revised at any time; there is no finished or published state that locks it.
The book's content is a set of notes, and a note can link to any other note.
A chapter is an ordered arrangement of notes chosen by the author.
Every saved change to a block is kept as a revision.

history.text: Every saved change to a note is kept as a revision.
history.reason: Content is stored as blocks, so revisions are kept per block.

requirements.text: The author can read any earlier revision of a note.
Markdown syntax typed in the editor becomes the matching blocks.

history.reason: Content is stored as blocks, not Markdown text; Markdown remains the way the author writes.

requirements.text: Inline LaTeX in a note is rendered as typeset maths.
Code blocks in the languages in `book.code-languages` are shown with syntax highlighting.
A note's content is an ordered list of blocks, not a Markdown text.
Each block is its own database row.
